LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS: FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.8: Phonological Awareness: Fluency

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Phonological Awareness: Fluency. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you do on different days of the week?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate pronunciation to outline the days of the week
2. respond to simple instructions correctly
3. appreciate the value of time for lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS: FLUENCY
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Phonological Awareness: Fluency helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS: FLUENCY
Study Phonological Awareness: Fluency like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Use appropriate pronunciation to outline the days of the week

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate pronunciation to outline the days of the week. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate pronunciation to outline the days of the week.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Phonological Awareness: Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate pronunciation to outline the days of the week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to simple instructions correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to simple instructions correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to simple instructions correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Phonological Awareness: Fluency to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to simple instructions correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the value of time for lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the value of time for lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the value of time for lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the value of time for lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Phonological Awareness: Fluency is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Phonological Awareness: Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use appropriate pronunciation to outline the days of the week)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Phonological Awareness: Fluency to a partner. (skill: respond to simple instructions correctly)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the value of time for lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Phonological Awareness: Fluency to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use appropriate pronunciation to outline the days of the week.
3. Practise this skill: respond to simple instructions correctly.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the value of time for lifelong learning.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Phonological Awareness: Fluency from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Phonological Awareness: Fluency: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Phonological Awareness: Fluency?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you do on different days of the week?
2. Why are instructions important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Phonological Awareness: Fluency means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use appropriate pronunciation to outline the days of the week.
5. Be able to: respond to simple instructions correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
